facts.fact: NIRA announced in late October 2026 that its Hubiye platform is implemented, letting service providers verify ID credentials against its database by a one-time password sent to the ID holder.

UNDP reported in May 2026 that Hubiye supported real-time identity verification across 25 integrated services including commercial banking, and the government directed public-facing service providers to integrate with it in April 2025.
NIRA launched the eAqoonsi app in May 2025, which gives citizens a digital version of their national ID that authorities encourage them to use to access services.

systems.tiers: OTP consent by SMS or email

SOM.note: Gives a 2029 enrolment target of 15 million and 1.2 million citizens served by Hubiye, not people enrolled.
Nothing on who operates or owns the system.
Names banking and unnamed services checking the ID, which is verification, not a public register keyed on the number.
No statement of unique numbers issued, biometrics or certification.

facts.fact: NIRA says service providers verify ID credentials against its national database through Hubiye, with a provider submitting the ID number and the holder authorising by one-time password.
The document says Hubiye serves banking and public services, and UNDP counted 25 integrated services including commercial banking in May 2026.
UNDP reported in May 2026 that Hubiye served 25 integrated services and about 1.2 million citizens.
